correctness.rationale: The cube-section inradius is (1-a^2)^(-1/2) for ordered |normal| coordinates a<=b<=c: strip normals in the section have squared lengths 1-a_i^2, and a central ball attains the optimum by symmetrization. Enumerating cube-edge vertices gives Z=(a+b)/c if c>=a+b, or (c-a)/b otherwise. Haar spherical area in h=a/sqrt(b^2+c^2), theta=atan(b/c) is (1+h^2)^(-3/2)dh dtheta on asin h<=theta<=pi/4, establishing the uniform conditional angle and f_H. The two monotone branches invert to L_h/R_h, giving the stated conditional CDF. Their endpoint values yield sharp piecewise support transitions h0 and 1/sqrt5; differentiating inverse angles cancels the h-dependent numerators in the overlap. I independently calculated five 40,000-angle midpoint conditional CDF comparisons at h=0.2, all within 1/40000. The infinite law follows from analytic geometry, not the finite check. Boundary at h=0 and regular hexagon at h=1/sqrt2 treated separately.
